title: Experimental paper skim notes — modular evals & kernels
content:
High-level: quick skims of 3 papers and some half-baked experiments to try on the serving runtime. These are light reading notes; intent is to capture operationally-relevant ideas rather than deep proofs.

Paper picks (fast pass):
1) Sparse attention + chunked kernels (arXiv 2905.01234) — idea: split attention into local + occasional global tokens. They show consistent inference speedups when sequence > 8k on A100-ish hardware by reorganizing matmuls and avoiding large softmaxes across full seq. Implementation note: would map cleanly to our dynamic-kernel selection layer (choose sparse kernel for long-context policies).
 - Takeaway: add a runtime policy that inspects sequence length histogram and switches to sparse-local kernels when > N tokens in tail (N ~= 4096 from paper).
 - Risk: output distribution shift for tasks that need global context (summarization). Need small QA/regression suite.

2) Lightweight KV-compression for continuous decoding (NeurIPS 2028 proceedings) — compresses KV by low-rank projection per layer every M steps; decompose then reconstruct on demand. Claims ~2x memory reduction with <1% perplexity delta.
 - Engineer thought: combine with our prefix cache to store compressed KVs for older prefixes; reconstruct only for hits with high reuse probability. Could reduce memory pressure on Dedicated pools.
 - Experiment idea: instrument a dedicated pod with compressed-KV option and run streaming-chat workload for 48h to measure token throughput and realtime latency tail.

3) Kernel autotuning for quantized models (MLSys 2029 short) — autotuner that picks kernel variant per (sequence_len, batch_size, quant_mode) using offline traces + small on-host microbenchmarks. Gains ~15% latency reduction vs static selection.
 - Ops implication: add a small-onstart benchmark step to Dedicated instance boot that samples representative (seq,batch,quant) tuples from recent traffic and caches kernel map.
 - Tradeoffs: boot time increase vs steady-state latency improvement. Also compatibility testing for model variants.

Quick experiments to prioritize (order by expected impact / low friction):
A) Sequence-histogram-based kernel switch (prototype in Python runtime shim) — 2d feature: avg_seq_length and tail_95. If tail_95 > 4096 enable sparse-local kernels. Run against two workloads (summarize-news, chat-typing). Measure p50/p95/p99 latency and perplexity on small eval set.
B) Compressed-KV prefix cache toggle — implement a conversion layer that stores compressed KV for prefixes older than 30s; reconstruct on hit. Target: 30% memory saving on long-chat traces with <2% quality regression.
C) Local autotune microbench on boot — add 10s microbench across 4 kernel variants for (seq=512,1024,2048) and quant modes (fp16, int8). Persist mapping in metadata and compare to baseline static selection.

Metrics to capture for each run (minimum):
 - throughput (tokens/sec) sustained over 1h and 24h
 - latency p50/p95/p99 for token generation
 - end-to-end quality probes (small eval set: 200 prompts) — use BLEU/ROUGE for summarization and accuracy for question-answering slices
 - memory residency (GPU memory usage over time) and host paging events
 - failure/retry counts and any model fallback triggers

Open questions / TODOs: 
 - How to label "global context_required" prompts in live traffic? Heuristic: messages with keywords ("compare", "overview", "history") + long input length. Might need a simple classifier (tiny transformer) to avoid blind sparse-switch.
 - Compatibility matrix: which open models in our catalog already support sparse kernels? Need mapping. @Maya to extract catalog metadata (model architecture, supported execution paths).
 - Safety: any decoding artifacts introduced by compression (e.g., token repetition spikes)? Add a short burst detection metric.

Notes for integration w/ Console and Optimize:
 - Expose kernel-selection policy as per-route toggle in Console (so customers can opt-in/opt-out). Default: off for hosted tier; on for Dedicated with opt-in.
 - Optimize feature: surface estimated unit-cost delta and expected latency change for suggested switches (we can compute offline from microbench traces).

Short experiments plan timeline (1 sprint = 2 weeks):
 - Sprint 0 (setup): instrumentation for sequence histograms + small eval harness (bench framework).
 - Sprint 1: prototype A (sequence-histogram kernel switch) — internal traffic only.
 - Sprint 2: prototype B (compressed KV) — lab tests with long-chat traces.
 - Sprint 3: integrate autotune microbench (pilot Dedicated instance).

Slack/PRs to create:
 - #eng-serving-runtime post: "experiment: sparse-kernel-by-tail-length" (include brief description, measurement plan)
 - PR: runtime/profiles add sequence-histogram/decision-point (WIP) — link above in linked_artifacts PR 482 is placeholder.

Random heuristics/brain-dump (save for later):
 - If compressed-KV reconstruction is costly for cold-cache hits, consider hybrid: store full for top-K prefixes (by frequency) and compressed for long-tail.
 - Trigger strategy: try gradual rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if p99 latency increases > 10% or quality regression > 3% on probes.

End-of-note quick checklist:
 - [ ] Create small eval set for summarization and QA (200 prompts)
 - [ ] Add sequence-histogram telemetry to runtime traces (low-overhead counters)
 - [ ] Wire up boot microbench harness for Dedicated images
 - [ ] Ask Maya for model capability export (sparse/quant support)
 - [ ] Schedule 4h sync with infra to discuss Dedicated boot-time tradeoffs

Personal reflection: these papers feel operational — not a need to reimplement full algorithms, but to translate key knobs (sparse/local vs global, compressed KV, autotune) into pragmatic runtime toggles. The next step: pick one small prototype (A) and get numbers.
